# Getting an account (your PI must do this) {#sec-account}

::: {.tldr}
You cannot request your own ARCC account. A **PI** (UW faculty or research scientist) must
request it against a specific **project**, in writing. No project means no account. Non-UW
collaborators get restricted "ARCC-Only" accounts with real limitations. Sort this out
first — it commonly blocks new performers for weeks.
:::

## How accounts work

ARCC will not create an account without written confirmation from a Principal Investigator
who owns a project. Accounts are tied to funded projects for accounting and fair-share
purposes.

So the first step is a conversation, not a form:

> "Which project am I being added to, and can the PI email ARCC to add me?"

For ASCEND/ARID performers the project is something like `cowy-firesurro` (the project this
guide was written under). Confirm the exact project name with your PI — you type it into
**every job** you run (@sec-anatomy).

## Who can be a PI

- UW **faculty** (extended-term / tenure-track) or a **Research Scientist**.
- **Not** adjunct, **not** emeritus, **not** a postdoc or student.

If your advisor doesn't qualify, someone who does must sponsor the project. This matters for
a multi-institution engine like ASCEND, where the leader of your sub-project might not be UW
faculty.

## UW accounts vs. ARCC-Only accounts

ASCEND spans UW, CSU, CU Boulder, Mines, NCAR, and NEON, so this distinction affects
collaborators:

| | Full UW account | ARCC-Only account |
|---|---|---|
| Who | UW-affiliated people | External collaborators without a UW identity |
| HPC (MedicineBow) | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitLab | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Globus data transfer** | ✅ | ❌ **cannot use Globus** |
| Other UW services | ✅ | ❌ |

::: {.callout-warning}
## ARCC-Only accounts and Globus
External collaborators on ARCC-Only accounts **cannot use Globus**, the recommended way to
move large datasets (@sec-moving-data). They'll need a *guest collection* set up for them,
or a UW person to broker transfers. Plan for this early if your data lives at CSU or NCAR.
:::

## The free tier

Each researcher's baseline allocation:

- **100,000 CPU core-hours per year**
- **20,000 GPU-hours per year**

That is plenty for getting started — 100,000 core-hours is roughly one 96-core node running
flat out for six weeks. Larger allocations and investor projects exist beyond this.
Core-hours are counted as (cores × wall-clock hours), a reason not to over-ask for resources
(@sec-resources).

## The practical checklist

1. Confirm with your PI **which project** you're joining and its exact name.
2. Have the **PI email `arcc-help@uwyo.edu`** to request your account on that project.
   (You emailing them yourself won't work — they need the PI's confirmation.)
3. Once ARCC provisions you, you'll get a UW username. Your first login is @sec-first-login.
4. If you're an external collaborator, flag it now and ask how you'll move data, since
   Globus won't be available to you.

No VPN is required to reach ARCC, on campus or off, so once your account exists you can log
in from anywhere.
